Extracting audio from video with ffmpeg

Source: vignettes/ffmpeg_wav.Rmd
ffmpeg_wav.Rmd

This vignette shows how to pull the audio track out of a folder of video files and write it to WAV files ready for acoustic analysis. os_prep_audio() wraps ffmpeg to extract and convert an audio stream to the format openSMILE expects; running it across many files in parallel is a matter of pairing it with furrr.

library(openac)
library(future)
library(furrr)

First confirm that openac can find a working ffmpeg (see set_ffmpeg() if not):

check_ffmpeg()

List the input videos and derive a matching WAV path for each output:

infiles <- list.files(
  path = "Z:/DynAMoS/Stimuli/Video",
  pattern = "\\.mp4$",
  full.names = TRUE,
  recursive = TRUE
)

# Mirror the input paths into an Audio/ folder, swapping the extension.
outfiles <- gsub("/Stimuli/Video/", "/Stimuli/Audio/", infiles)
outfiles <- gsub("\\.mp4$", ".wav", outfiles)

Set a parallel plan and map os_prep_audio() over the input/output pairs:

plan("multisession", workers = 4)

future_walk2(
  .x = infiles,
  .y = outfiles,
  .f = os_prep_audio
)

For this common “every file in a directory” case you can skip the manual file bookkeeping entirely and let os_prep_audio_dir() find, pair, and process the files for you. A file that fails does not stop the run: it is warned about, recorded as "failed", and the remaining files still go through. The returned data frame records the outcome of every file:

os_prep_audio_dir(
  indir = "Z:/DynAMoS/Stimuli/Video",
  inext = "mp4",
  outdir = "Z:/DynAMoS/Stimuli/Audio",
  recursive = TRUE
)

Finally, confirm the WAV files were written:

list.files(path = "Z:/DynAMoS/Stimuli/Audio", pattern = "\\.wav$")
